items.title: Separate opening hours, not break time

labels.name: Opening Hours
labels.description: Business Hours, off time, holidays, seasonal

items.body:
I recently tried to load the opening hours for a business and found that the app would not record the split time.

In my logic, and following the scheme indicated by OSM to save a split schedule, for example: from 08:00 to 12:00 and from 16:00 to 20:00 (opening_hours=Mo-Fr 08:00-12:00,16:00-20:00) the app did not take the period from 16:00 to 20:00.

I reported the situation as a bug to tech support, and Alexander Borsuk Software Engineer & Co-Founder @ Organic Maps very kindly and patiently replied that the schedule should be loaded like this: opening hours from 8:00 to 20:00, and then add a break from 12:00 to 16:00.

I consider that the way Organic Maps proposes in its app to load the schedules is not the natural way used by OSM mappers, those of us who think in terms of the formal scheme proposed by OSM.

In many countries, work schedules are not on a straight timetable and businesses operate on a split timetable.

In fact, other mapping apps use the OSM scheme to load schedules.

I invite developers to analyze the possibility of changing the way of loading opening hours, accordi
![horas](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6495550/225609623-90fd828d-d624-42ff-8af0-47aeff3fd0f5.jpeg)
ng to the OSM scheme.

I attach an illustrative image of the opening hours of a local business in Argentina.

items.title: [Android] Opening hours UI rework
items.body:
Another week, another PR!

Closes Issue #970. Made Android Opening hours UI simmilar to iOS. `opening_hours` value matches different cases:

## Case 1: Label only
E.g.
* `opening_hours = 24/7`
* `opening_hours` unparsable

🌍 https://osm.org/node/3882420485 → 🕗 `24/7`
🌍 https://osm.org/node/6070463188 → 🕗 Unparsed `Mo-Fr 09:00-19:00; Sa,Su,PH 09:00-20:00`

Show just label:

![case1_24-7](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/720808/142868144-f8366182-cd2d-42a0-92ad-5674208643be.png)

Unparsable sample:

![case1_unparsable](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/720808/142868176-afd20e44-fb5e-4427-8691-c0d3021945a6.png)

## Case 2: Label + time
E.g.
* `opening_hours = 10:00-22:00`
* `opening_hours = Mo-Su 17:00-00:00`

🌍 https://osm.org/node/4601505099 → 🕗`Mo-Su 17:00-00:00`

Open hours are right aligned:

![case2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/720808/142868232-b3d3c620-753e-4761-b47b-54b7b61b4b88.png)

## Case 3: Label + time + non-business time(s)
E.g.
* `opening_hours = 10:00-16:00, 16:30-22:00`
* `opening_hours = Mo-Su 10:00-16:00, 16:30-22:00`

🌍 https://osm.org/node/6293418985 → 🕗`Mo-Su 9:30-14:00, 15:00-18:30`

Open hours are right aligned. Non-business hours text below hours.

![case3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/720808/142868314-9f56382c-3df9-4dd7-afea-600d8e348989.png)

## Case 4: Label + time + week schedule
E.g.
* `opening_hours = Mo-Fr 09:00-20:00; Sa 10:00-17:00; Su 11:00-14:00`

🌍 https://osm.org/way/684433599 → 🕗`Mo-Fr 06:00-22:00; Sa-Su 07:00-22:00`

Open hours are right aligned for today and for the whole week.

![case4](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/720808/142868382-52f95611-30f3-44c9-bcc2-cdac8e6c7f7f.png)

## Case 5: Label + time + week schedule + non-business time(s)
E.g.
* `opening_hours = Mo-Fr 09:00-15:00,15:30-22:00; Sa 10:00-15:00,15:30-22:00; Su 10:00-18:00`

🌍 https://osm.org/node/2665722353 → 🕗`Mo-Th 13:30-16:00,20:30-23:30;Tu off;Fr,Sa 13:30-16:00,20:30-24:00;Su 13:30-16:00`

Open hours are right aligned for today and for the whole week. Non-business hours text below hours for today and for each week day.

![case5](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/720808/142868620-648e36f5-697c-44b8-b75d-4447ba4f1275.png)

## Case 6: Closed today label + week schedule + non-business time(s)
E.g.
* `opening_hours = Mo off; Tu-Fr 09:00-15:00,15:30-22:00; Sa 10:00-15:00,15:30-22:00; Su 10:00-18:00`

🌍 https://osm.org/node/2199786968 → 🕗`Th,Fr 21:30-00:30,Sa 14:00-17:00,21:30-00:30; Mo-We off`

Label tells that POI is closed today in red. Open hours are right aligned for the whole week. Non-business hours text below hours for each week day.

![case6](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/720808/142868691-d7e7d439-7c83-41fb-968f-28f82ee06f13.png)

## Layout changes:

**Before:**
![layout_old](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/720808/142869473-aabbcc99-c8d8-40d3-9e41-33aea072884f.png)

**After:**
![layout_new](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/720808/142869507-a4572cfc-a757-4152-8799-4c9886f79dcf.png)

## Questions:

* ☑️ Do we need horizontal separators as iOS version does? - No
* ☑️ Does Opening hours widget should be collapsible like iOS version? - No
* ☑️ iOS version shows if place is closed at some date. See "Sun-Wed closed" at the Case 6 screenshot. Do we need the same feature for Android? - Added

## Update 23 Nov 2021

Added em-dash as open time and non-business time separator. (I will not update all screenshots in this PR. Just belive me 😄)

Added closed weekdays as last item of week schedule:

![android_new_case5_case6_plus](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/720808/143013035-b71baf1b-d8e6-4b12-b6ab-53d45b7ff658.png)

items.title: support opening_hours:drive_through

labels.name: Opening Hours
labels.description: Business Hours, off time, holidays, seasonal

items.body:
Many fast-food restraunts and banks (at least in the USA) have separate lobby hours from drive through hours.

When the drive through hours are different, the key "opening_hours:drive_through" can be used to denote the different (often longer) hours that the drive through is open. 

For this reason, I recommend that Organic Maps support the tag opening_hours:drive_through to allow users to see when a restaurant's drive through is open, even when the lobby is closed.

items.title: [editor] Fix parsing of 'off' opening hours

labels.name: Opening Hours
labels.description: Business Hours, off time, holidays, seasonal

items.body:
This PR fixes the parsing of the "opening hours" strings that start with an "off" statement.

One example of opening hours not being processed correctly is the opening_hours tag `Mo off; Tu-Su 12:00-16:30, 19:00-24:00` of [this restaurant in OSM](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/9592619990).

Current opening hours parsing implementation does not like "off" statements if they are located in the first place, so this PR reorders the statements by placing the "off" ones at the end of the list.

This PR closes [PR 1612](https://github.com/organicmaps/organicmaps/issues/1612)

labels.name: Generator

labels.name: Opening Hours
labels.description: Business Hours, off time, holidays, seasonal

items.body:
Found opening-hours that should have been parsed: `Mo-Sa 07:00–18:00; Su 09:00-14:00` (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/5022879262)
on closer inspection, the dash between Mo & Sa is actually an [En Dash](https://unicode-table.com/en/2013/) instead of a standard [Hyphen-Minus](https://unicode-table.com/en/002D/).
technically this is an OSM data issue, but it would be good to handle it.

need to convert all similar dashes in the generator (although not characters within quotation marks):
`‐` HYPHEN 
`‑` NON-BREAKING HYPHEN
`‒` FIGURE DASH
`–` EN DASH
`﹘`SMALL EM DASH
`۔‎`  ARABIC FULL STOP
`⁃` HYPHEN BULLET
`˗` MODIFIER LETTER MINUS SIGN
`−` MINUS SIGN
`➖` HEAVY MINUS SIGN
`Ⲻ` COPTIC CAPITAL LETTER DIALECT-P NI

(similar characters found from https://www.unicode.org/Public/security/15.0.0/confusables.txt)

items.title: [android] Opening hours preview for places

labels.name: Beta
labels.description: PRs ready to be tested before merging them to master, or issues found in beta versions.

items.body: Add a preview of the schedule of a place at the top of the page, indicating if it's closed or open, with the time remaining before it closes or opens. The behavior should be exactly the same as the current implementation on iOS, as I tried to follow as much as possible the implementation that was proposed in #3045. - Closes #1852 - Closes #1688 Changes: - Added JNI bindings for the `OpeningHours::InfoT` struct (translated as `OpeningHoursInfo` in java) - Created `OpeningHours.nativeGetOpeningHoursInfoFromString` in java to get the result of `OpeningHours::GetInfo` - Marked some ios translations to also be on android Tests made: - android with api level 36 and 28 - tested many places on many dates - tested with places that are open 24/7 There are two issues with the current implementation: - If you look at the time remaining before a place open *before* a time change, but the place opens *after* the time change, the result is wrong by one hour (fortunately I had a lot of luck and tested it on the right day). I'm not sure how to handle this edge case, nor if it's even possible to do so in a clean way, since it looks like even `java.util.Calendar` is confused about it. I can't test myself if the bug also exists with the iOS implementation. - For places with weird schedule format that isn't parsed properly by the app, it sometimes display "open" or "closed". But it is likely a problem inside the native function `OpeningHours::GetInfo` and should be handled in a separate PR. Screenshots:

**Describe the issue**

When opening hours string ends with `; Su,PH off `, Organic Maps incorrectly believes that Su is open instead of closed.

**Steps to reproduce**

A shop located at 34.680329, 33.040013 has the following opening_hours:

```
Mo-Tu,Th-Fr 09:00-19:00; We,Sa 09:00-14:00; Su,PH off
```

Organic Maps incorrectly shows that the shop is open on Sunday all day. 

**Expected behavior**

Organic Maps should see that Su is off. The string above is parsed correctly at https://openingh.ypid.de/evaluation_tool/ and OsmAnd also shows the schedule for this shop as expected (closed on Sunday).

items.title: Fix sub-minute opening hours countdown
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #13576, where Organic Maps could show **"opens in 0 minutes"** when a place was actually going to open in less than a minute.

For example, if a place opens at **09:00** and the current time is **08:59:30**, there are 30 seconds left, but the countdown was calculated using integer division:

`30 / 60 = 0`

So the UI displayed **"opens in 0 minutes"**.

## What I changed

While tracing the opening-hours flow, I found that the countdown was calculated in two different ways:

* Search results use the C++ `MinutesUntilTransition()` helper.
* Android and iOS place pages independently calculate `(nextTime - currentTime) / 60`.

I fixed the shared C++ calculation so that a **future transition within 1–59 seconds is shown as 1 minute**, while keeping the existing minute-flooring behavior for longer durations.

I also applied the same fix to the Android and iOS place-page calculations.

I intentionally did **not** use ceiling division. For example, `59m 59s` must remain `59 minutes`, rather than becoming `60 minutes`, because the existing UI has boundaries based on the 60-minute value.

## Regression coverage

Added compile-time checks for the important boundaries:

* 1s, 30s, 59s → 1 minute
* 60s, 61s → 1 minute
* 3599s → 59 minutes
* 3600s → 60 minutes
* transition at/past current time → 0
* unknown/sentinel value remains unchanged

The C++ regression checks pass.

## Testing

* C++ regression checks: **passed**
* Android tests: **not run** — Android SDK was not available in the development environment
* iOS tests: **not run** — Xcode was not available in the development environment

The final change is limited to the C++ countdown calculation and the corresponding Android/iOS place-page calculations.

items.title: [opening_hours] Keep spaced time lists under their weekday selector
items.body:
Fix the next opening time for [OSM node 14132311401](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/14132311401), tagged `We-Sa 09:00-13:00 , 14:30-19:00`: on Monday, the iOS preview should report Wednesday at 09:00 instead of today at 14:30.

Skip whitespace before a comma inside a time list, keeping both spans under the same weekday selector. Restore the parser position when no time span follows so additional rules still parse correctly. Use an explicit `open` modifier in the additional-rule serialization test instead of relying on whitespace to change the meaning.

Validation:

- macOS arm64 Debug: `opening_hours_tests` and `editor_tests` pass via CTest.
- Regression coverage includes all four comma-spacing combinations, round trips, explicit additional rules, and the reported feature's next opening time.
- Corpus comparison: 17 existing parses change, 12 rejected values become accepted, zero accepted values become rejected; 17 controls for selectors, modifiers, comments and other separators retain their behavior.
